articles.title: Trump openly ridiculed live on German TV as World Cup broadcasters let loose
articles.description: German broadcasters mocked President Donald Trump and FIFA President Gianni Infantino live during the World Cup final after Trump was handed the tournament trophy to present. On Sunday, Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to attend a World Cup final, where Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. Officials brought the World Cup trophy to Trump in the FIFA president's private box before kickoff, and he was seen holding it in his lap. "Well, that's a violation of the rules," one host for the German public broadcaster Zweites Deutsches Fernsehen said on air. "Trump and Infantino — those two were made for each other," a second host added. "Fascinated by power and themselves, too." ZDF commentator Oliver Schmidt went further during the broadcast. "And there is the U.S. President and his telephone joker on the right — his lackey, Gianni Infantino," Schmidt said. The phrase "telephone joker" referred to Trump's call to Infantino earlier in the tournament to request that FIFA review a red-card suspension handed to U.S. striker Folarin Balogun. FIFA lifted the suspension — the first time since 1962 that a red card at a World Cup did not result in a ban. Some fans inside MetLife Stadium booed Trump when he appeared on the stadium's screens. During Spain's trophy celebration on the field, Infantino was seen guiding Trump off the stage. "They can edit him out of that," Spanish broadcaster Claudio Fabiano said on air as Trump photobombed the national team's celebrations. Trump told Fox Sports before the match that he wanted the United States to host the World Cup again. "We have to do this again," he said. "And we have to do it while I'm around."

articles.title: Trump-loving Argentina president becomes 'laughing stock' after World Cup tweet misfire
articles.description: Argentine President Javier Milei ignited howls of laughter after firing off a celebratory tweet — moments after his nation suffered a pulverizing loss to Spain in the 2026 World Cup championship. The Donald Trump ally apparently neglected to unschedule a victory tweet Sunday and announced to his followers plans to celebrate the Argentine National Team, which fell 1-0 to Spain and became the first team in World Cup final history that did not attempt a shot on goal in regulation time in World Cup final history. "WORLD CELEBRATION," Milei crowed on X. "Given the concern about the celebrations for the achievement reached by the Argentine National Team, I inform the population that, depending on what the Players and the Technical Staff decide regarding the day to celebrate, it will be declared a national holiday." Milei had announced before the game that he would not attend, citing his personal superstitions, but he declared a national holiday afterward for what turned out to be a runner-up finish for soccer legend Lionel Messi's likely last World Cup appearance. "Embarrassing. Milei neglected to unschedule his victory tweet declaring an Argentina national holiday to celebrate the World Cup win Netanyahu promised him," slammed former Federal Reserve banker Kathleen Tyson. "Oops." "Javier Milei becomes the laughingstock of the world: he forgot to delete a scheduled tweet announcing Argentina's victory and a subsequent public holiday... even though the team lost the final," posted French media outlet Focus. "What are you celebrating man? You guys lost?" wondered widely followed X user Dr. Parik Patel.

articles.title: Iran says that diplomatic efforts have been "active" in recent days, received proposals from several mediators
articles.description: The good news at least is that there is some form of exchange in order to try and de-escalate, with Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Baghaei insisting that a "binary choice of negotiations or war is not useful". He maintains that "diplomacy does not negate defense" and that "defense is not incompatible with diplomacy". Adding that Iran has received several proposals from mediators for the resumption of negotiations. As much as the headlines might point to some return to optimism, it is still too early to prejudge anything. As mentioned before, nuclear/uranium negotiations are not going to amount to anything as there are still key red lines that are holding for both sides. And in the bigger picture, this is exactly what Iran wants. That is to keep playing for time and to drag all of this out over and over and for as long as they can. From before: Iran's strategy in leveraging on control over the Strait of Hormuz looks to be working Baghaei goes on to say that US talks might be possible if and only if though they are pursued on the basis of national interests. As much as both sides can talk the talk, I can foresee negotiations breaking down again the minute missile strikes are exchanged once more. And with Iran not going to relent on giving up control over the Strait of Hormuz, I don't see how things will be any much different from what they were in the past few weeks. If anything, it could just be a case of Groundhog Day for markets as we continue to repeatedly take one step back and then one foot forward again. This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.
